source.question: q-157692
source.value:
A differentiable equation is *separable* if it can be written in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=h(x)g(y).
$$

If an equation is separable, we say that the variables are *separated* when it is written in the form

$$
\frac{1}{g(y)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=h(x).
$$

Notice that our differentiable equation is separable since it can be written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}\cdot {e}^{y}
$$

Therefore, we separate the variables as follows:

$$
\frac{1}{{e}^{y}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x},
$$

or, equivalently,

$$
{e}^{-y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}.
$$

decisions.question: q-154359

source.question: q-154359
source.value: Find the general solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2x}{{e}^{y}}.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: q-154359

source.question: q-154359
source.value:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2x}{{e}^{y}} \\ {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\text{d}y & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{y} & ={x}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
{e}^{y}={x}^{2}+C.
$$

source.value: Find the general solution to the differential equation ${y}^{′}={y}^{2}+1.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: q-14257

source.question: q-14257
source.value:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={y}^{2}+1 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={y}^{2}+1 \\ \frac{1}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}y & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{arctan}⁡(y) & =x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\operatorname{arctan}⁡(y)=x+C.
$$

We're required to write the solution in the form $y=y(x).$ By doing this, we get

$$
y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(x+C).
$$

source.value: Find the general solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)y=0$ for $y\ne 0.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: q-8305

source.question: q-8305
source.value:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)y & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)y \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}y & =\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|y| & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡|y|=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C.
$$

We're required to write the solution in the form $y=y(x).$ By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡|y| & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C \\ |y| & ={e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C} \\ |y| & ={e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot {e}^{C} \\ |y| & =K{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

where $K={e}^{C}$ and $K>0.$

We can drop the absolute value bars by allowing $K$ to be either positive or negative. Therefore, the most general solution is

$$
y=K{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.
$$

source.value: Find the general solution to the differential equation ${y}^{′}-\sqrt{y}=2x\sqrt{y}$ for $y\ne 0.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: q-8303

source.question: q-8303
source.value:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}-\sqrt{y} & =2x\sqrt{y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-\sqrt{y} & =2x\sqrt{y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x\sqrt{y}+\sqrt{y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(2x+1)\sqrt{y} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(2x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\,\text{d}y & =\int (2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\ 2\sqrt{y} & ={x}^{2}+x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
2\sqrt{y}={x}^{2}+x+C
$$

We're required to write the solution in the form $y=y(x).$ By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={(\frac{{x}^{2}+x+C}{2})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
